solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Moving miles with a clean mixture

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new order, signalling a rearrangement of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone shifting a few miles with a tidy assortment of belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges MILES and A CLEAN together into the eleven-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany or assorted collection of items is a mixture of things.

clue.text: Smallest room at the bottom of one grand northern home

indicators.note: in a down entry, being at the bottom means coming after the other letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
the smallest room is a jokey name for the toilet, the loo

explanation.surface: A grand northern house with its tiny toilet tucked downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand northern home' reads as a mansion, but 'grand' is just G.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is a dwelling of the far north.

clue.text: Catch one prize for crew member

parts.note: to cop is to catch
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lot is something won by lottery, a prize or allotted portion

explanation.surface: Catching one prize-winning member of a boat crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The second pilot on a flight deck is one of the aircraft's crew.

clue.text: Spring time that's longer than the annual average

definitions.text: that's longer than the annual average
definitions.note: the definition describes one that runs longer than usual

parts.note: a spring is a leap or jump
a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: A spring season that lasts longer than in an ordinary year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring time' reads as the season, but it is two charade pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Every fourth year has 366 days, one more than the normal calendar count.

clue.text: One's temporarily welcoming home

indicators.note: the words welcome the letters inside them, holding them within

explanation.surface: Someone is temporarily taking a guest into their home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is its home, and the word means a cosy dwelling generally.

clue.text: Get a role playing, for example, Mr Hyde

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: An actor lands a part playing Mr Hyde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks theatrical, fitting 'role', but it scrambles GET A ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's second self, the classic example of a hidden other personality.

clue.text: Every other letter an A? Awkward!

indicators.note: awkward letters are put into a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: A writer complains that every second character being an A is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every other letter' tempts as a selection instruction; 'Every other' is the definition, and LETTER AN A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate as an adjective means every second one, as in alternate days.

clue.text: It contains coal lawfully — and cash

parts.note: lawful, legal, in the clue's adverbial form standing for the adjective
a tender is the wagon behind a steam locomotive carrying its coal

explanation.surface: Something lawfully carrying coal, and money too.
explanation.walkthrough: A locomotive's tender is the truck holding its fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes and coins that must be accepted in payment of debts are official currency.

clue.text: Edrich initially dropped by Thomson's partner where French cricket might be played?

definitions.text: where French cricket might be played?

indicators.note: a letter dropped by a word is removed from it

parts.note: Dennis Lillee bowled in harness with Jeff Thomson for Australia in the 1970s

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the name Edrich

explanation.surface: A cricket tale: England batsman Edrich dropped off the bowling of Thomson's fast-bowling partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E (Edrich's first letter) from LILLEE. French cricket is a children's garden game; the joke is that any cricket in a French city is French cricket. Lillee and Thomson were a feared Australian bowling pair; John Edrich batted for England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a city in northern France, so cricket played there would literally be French cricket.

clue.text: The planes needing repair — jumbos

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: The aircraft are faulty: the jumbo jets need fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbos' looks like jets after 'planes', but it means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was a famous circus elephant, and the name became a general nickname for the big animal.

clue.text: What might precede tavern in the town in May, perhaps?

definitions.text: What might precede tavern in the town
definitions.meaning: the old song title runs 'There is a tavern in the town', so the phrase there's a comes before those words
... May, UK Prime Minister 2016-19, is an example of someone with this first name

explanation.surface: A query about which pub in a town might come first in the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as THERE'S A it precedes the words of the song 'There is a tavern in the town'; read as one name it is the first name of Prime Minister Theresa May.
explanation.definitionFit: The old drinking song opens with these words, and the same letters make the first name of a British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Fired every gun shot on court

definitions.meaning: firing all guns at once is discharging a salvo
in tennis a ball hit before it bounces is struck on the full

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is military, firing a salvo; the other is tennis, hitting the ball before it lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley is both a simultaneous discharge of guns and a tennis stroke hit before the bounce.

clue.text: Vogue's first with trendy feather dressing

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the magazine name

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
an aigrette is an ornamental tuft of feathers

explanation.surface: Vogue's latest fashion: a trendy feathered outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests clothing after Vogue and feathers; it is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil and vinegar mix poured over salad is a dressing.

clue.text: Anzac's JCBs?

parts.note: Australian and New Zealand soldiers are nicknamed after trench ..., and JCB excavators are mechanical earth-movers

explanation.walkthrough: JCB is a British maker of excavators; Anzacs, Australian and New Zealand troops, are nicknamed for the same word, so the machines are the soldiers' own namesakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the excavating machines and the antipodean soldiers share this nickname.

clue.text: Prisoner cut short time in cyberspace

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: an internee is a person held in custody without trial, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A prisoner's sentence trimmed, with his time served online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last E off INTERNEE to leave INTERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the virtual realm of the global computer network, the online world.

clue.text: Spruce in Cologne — a Tannenbaum

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A spruce tree in Cologne is a Tannenbaum, the German Christmas fir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the tree, given the German Tannenbaum, but it is the adjective meaning tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce as an adjective means smart and tidy in appearance.

clue.text: Shy member of the family?

parts.note: a shy is a fairground stall where things are thrown at a target, and the figure thrown at is a relative's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid; at a British fairground a shy is a throwing game, and this figure was the target, now meaning anyone everyone attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground dummy pelted at a coconut shy was given a female relative's name.

clue.text: Flavouring Egon Ronay's cooking after chopping both ends

indicators.note: food that is cooking is being worked over, so these letters are mixed up
each of the two names loses its end letter

explanation.surface: A food critic's kitchen: Egon Ronay is cooking, after trimming the ends of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping both ends' cuts the last letter from each name, EGO + RONA, and 'cooking' rearranges EGORONA. Egon Ronay was a famous restaurant guide writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb such as marjoram's wild cousin is used as a flavouring in cooking.

clue.text: Very important lady carried in rickety old van across country

indicators.note: carried in means held inside the jumbled letters
a rickety vehicle is falling apart, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the most important lady

explanation.surface: The Queen being driven across country in a battered old van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' rearranges OLD VAN into OVLAND, and 'carried in' puts ER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by land rather than sea or air is going across country.

clue.text: US low-alcohol drink in local pub's ending all the time

parts.note: local means close by, near

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of pub

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A weak American beer always on tap at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local pub' reads as a British pub; 'local' gives NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt drink with almost no alcohol, sold in America during Prohibition.

clue.text: Favourite seated, but not in the middle

indicators.note: the central letters of the word are taken away

explanation.surface: The favoured guest was given a seat, but not in the middle of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in the middle' removes AT from the centre of SEATED.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a seeded player is one of the favourites, ranked to avoid other top players early.

clue.text: Difficult person like this — again!

parts.note: so can mean in this way, like this
again read as 'and so', the same word once more

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry about an awkward person behaving the same way yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this' gives SO, and 'again' adds the joining word and SO once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone this is a euphemism for a disagreeable or awkward individual.

clue.text: Collector at present in Greece

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: GR is the international abbreviation for Greece
present in the sense of being in this place, here

explanation.surface: A collector currently staying in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' tempts as a gift a collector might want; here it means being here, not elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gathers things, such as hunter-gatherers foraging food, collects them.

clue.text: One's highly vocal …!

parts.note: someone who yells loudly; also, printers' slang for the exclamation mark the clue itself ends on

explanation.walkthrough: The clue closes on the exclamation mark, which in typesetters' slang is called a screamer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who yells is highly vocal, and the punctuation mark shown is nicknamed the same.

clue.text: Musical composition — it's Fauré's final duet arranged

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of the composer's name
a musical arrangement reorders, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of music: Fauré's last work is an arranged duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' sounds musical but rearranges DUET after the E ending Fauré.
explanation.definitionFit: A study written to practise a technique is a short musical piece.

clue.text: Corresponded online about me having been ill

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word me runs backwards

parts.note: ailed means was unwell, having been ill

explanation.surface: Someone wrote over the internet about my recent illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', the surface sense, but it is the signal to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending electronic messages back and forth is corresponding over the internet.

clue.text: French sunrise

definitions.meaning: comedian ... French, of The Vicar of Dibley, gives the first name for her surname
daybreak, the first light of morning

explanation.walkthrough: 'French sunrise' reads as a sunrise in France; Dawn French is a British comic actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the moment the sun rises, and it is also the comedian's first name.

clue.text: 'A' students finish drink completely

parts.note: L is a learner, so LL is two learners or students
an end is a finish
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Top-grade students wrap up a drinking session by downing everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' is the letter itself; 'drink completely' tempts as one phrase but 'completely' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, as in 'beaten all ends up', means thoroughly or totally.

clue.text: Stock Exchange certificate St Paul found regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of the words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A share certificate was discovered at St Paul's.
explanation.walkthrough: Even letters of ST PAUL FOUND give T, A, L, O, N.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Stock Exchange this is the slip attached to a bond allowing new coupons to be claimed.

clue.text: Notes to accompany high-risk undertakings?

parts.note: notes are banknotes paid as extra wages for hazardous work, not written memos

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests written instructions; it means banknotes paid for risky work.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra pay given to workers for hazardous jobs is a recognised wage supplement.
